title: How property, football and politics link Manchester and Abu Dhabi

input.lead: A closer look at the relationship between Man City's owners and the Manchester political scene
input.summary: A closer look at the relationship between Man City's owners and the Manchester political scene
input.evidence_text: When Manchester City was found guilty in September of breaching Premier League financial rules, the damning and unprecedented verdict left the football world reeling An independent commission said the club had "systematically" broken rules between 2009 and 2018 by inflating sponsorship revenue to disguise secret funding of more than £830m into its football operations Speculation is now rife about the level of punishment City will face, although the club denies any wrongdoing and has appealed against the ruling While we await the outcome, the historical relationship between City's Abu Dhabi-based owners and Manchester's political elite - including the now Prime Minister Andy Burnham - has been in the spotlight There has been a focus on land deals, multimillion-pound regeneration schemes, and more recently, investigations into loans handed out to property companies owned ultimately by City's owner, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) Beyond the on-field success at the Eithad Stadium, what exactly is the Abu Dhabi story in Manchester?

input.summary: Ben Shelvin was once told he would never talk or walk ever again but found a unique way to bounce back

title: The case against each man accused of abusing woman drugged by husband

input.lead: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
input.summary: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
input.evidence_text: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004 before he began inviting strangers he met on online chatrooms, swinging websites and messaging apps to join him from about 2023 Here the BBC summarises the allegations against each man standing trial

title: Memorial lit up for first time in a century as part of North West Remembrance tributes

input.lead: The spectacle is just one of the many colourful tributes for Remembrance Day across north-west England
input.summary: The spectacle is just one of the many colourful tributes for Remembrance Day across north-west England
input.evidence_text: A neglected war memorial has been painstakingly restored by volunteers and lit up for the first time in its 104-year history ahead of Remembrance Day The Grade II* listed Hoylake and West Kirby monument has been transformed thanks to 14 years of renovations by the Friends of Grange Hill and Wirral Borough Council The spectacle is just one of a range of colourful tributes and events ahead of Remembrance Sunday across north-west England They include a striking display of thousands of poppies and crosses on a roundabout in Leigh, Greater Manchester, while Poulton-le-Fylde in Lancashire, has a displayed more than a 1,000 yellow poppies to honour "forgotten heroines" who served their country The Hoylake and West Kirby restoration project began in 2012 after a visitor tried to bring his father, a military veteran, to the memorial but found access virtually impossible Years of neglect had left the site overgrown while the site's remembrance garden had almost disappeared

title: Johnny Marr guitar could fetch £30k at Wiltshire auction

input.lead: The Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster was played during Marr's time with British rock band The The
input.summary: The Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster was played during Marr's time with British rock band The The
input.evidence_text: A guitar used by Johnny Marr after his split from The Smiths could fetch up to £30,000 when it goes under the hammer next month The white Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster was played during Marr's time with British rock band The The which he joined in 1988, a year after leaving The Smiths Auctioneers Gardiner Houlgate said a private owner bought the guitar in 2020, with Marr - originally from Manchester - signing the guitar's headstock at the time and providing a handwritten postcard describing how it had been used The guitar will go on sale at the Gardiner Houlgate auction house in Corsham, Wiltshire, on 8 December where it is estimated to fetch between £20,000 and £30,000 Luke Hobbs, auctioneer at Gardiner Houlgate, said: "We're valuing this guitar at around £20,000 to £30,000 based on other recent sales of Johnny Marr's instruments "Marr's equipment is very popular with collectors and fans

title: Developer Urban Splash forced to pay £45m over Manchester fire safety works

input.summary: A building developer has been ordered to pay more than £45m to the government after fire safety defects were repaired in seven high-rise buildings The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in insp
input.evidence_text: A building developer has been ordered to pay more than £45m to the government after fire safety defects were repaired in seven high-rise buildings The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £51.1m paid from the government's Building Safety Fund (BSF) established after the disaster The buildings were not owned by Urban Splash at the time of the remediation work and no BSF money was paid to it. A spokesperson said the scale of the liability was "significant" The Department of Housing, Communities and Local Government brought a case to a specialist tribunal, seeking an order for the developer to contribute towards the cost of the works paid from the taxpayer-supported fund On Thursday, the tribunal ruled that more than £45.7m should be paid to the government by Urban Splash

He is 32 years old and has built up a good career in the city Like thousands of people in Greater Manchester, he lives in a house in multiple occupation (HMO). It's the only way he can afford to live in the city he loves It isn't the dream, but it works for Sean. Yet earlier in October, he received an email from the property management firm that looks after the HMO, telling him and his housemates to 'be safe' The email was prompted by a wave of anger, protest and vandalism targeting properties across Salford which were alleged to be HMOs accommodating asylum seekers. 'No HMO' was daubed on doors and walls in paint, while windows were bricked across the borough in October After the spate of attacks, the property managers told Sean and his housemates to report any concerns with police, but 'not to worry'. "When something like this comes up you are going to be more aware and agitated," he told the Manchester Evening News

A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. input.evidence_text: £1.5m boost as Manchester fintech brings automation to business loans - Prolific North Skip to content News Wise Owl gets another order of Our Farm Next Door News Data organisation appoints Vikas Shah Agency Reboot strengthens senior team £1.5m boost as Manchester fintech brings automation to business loans Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 A Manchester-based fintech company serving banks and specialist lenders has secured £1.5 million to automate the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwrite. Crediflow AI has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. The company uses AI to automate much of that work, which is typically spread across spreadsheets, PDFs, emails and other disconnected systems. Aggregating this data manually can sometimes take up to several days, but Crediflow says its platform reduces that time to between 10 and 30 minutes, giving credit teams more time to concentrate on critical tasks. READ MORE: Leeds financial tech consultancy merges with London cloud specialist In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts, a process the industry calls financial spreading, analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
